articles.title: ★ Apple Should Eliminate the App Icon ‘Squircle Jail’
articles.titleZh: 苹果应打破应用图标的“圆角矩形监狱”
articles.summary: 苹果强制所有应用图标采用统一的“圆角矩形”设计，这一策略正在扼杀应用的品牌辨识度。过去图标的形状往往是其最核心的视觉标志，但在当前的 iOS 设计规范下，形状差异已不复存在。作者强烈建议苹果放宽限制，允许开发者使用异形图标或动态形状，以恢复应用市场的视觉多样性。打破“圆角矩形监狱”不仅能激发设计创新，还能大幅提升用户体验的丰富度。
articles.summaryEn: Apple's strategy of enforcing a uniform "squircle" shape for all app icons is stifling brand recognition for applications. The shape of an icon used to be its most iconic visual element, but under current iOS design guidelines, shape differentiation no longer exists. The author strongly suggests that Apple relax these restrictions, allowing developers to use custom shapes or dynamic forms to restore visual diversity in the App Store. Breaking out of the "squircle jail" can spur design innovation and significantly enrich the user experience.
articles.reason: 犀利批判了苹果应用图标设计的同质化问题，为关注 UI/UX 设计和平台生态健康度的读者提供了深刻见解。

blocks.text: Paul Kafasis, in a post at Rogue Amoeba’s blog titled “Free the Icons”:

Apple’s prohibition on shapes is a step backward for both
usability and creativity in app icons. Icons are now harder to
distinguish because they’re no longer allowed to be distinctive.
But there’s no technical reason for it. Apple could, and should,
once again allow icons to take on a wide variety of shapes.

It’s clear that some people within Apple recognize that the
transition to Liquid Glass introduced mistakes. They also appear
to have the authority to fix those mistakes. Refinements to
Apple’s own icons in Golden Gate are a welcome course correction,
as is the much-celebrated Liquid Glass opacity slider. It’s time
to correct the mistake of banning icon shapes as well.

Apple should stop forcing every icon into the same squircle.
The squircles, I will point out, are not in and of themselves the problem. The problem would be the same with any mandated shape, like, e.g., VisionOS’s circles.
John Siracusa:

Squircle Jail is the worst design-related thing Apple has ever
done to Mac developers, and probably the worst icon-related thing
it has ever done, period. Incredibly developer-hostile.

If squircled icons are actually better, then let that design win
in the market. That’s how we transitioned from the classic Mac OS
icon style to the more photorealistic Mac OS X icon style.
Developers adopted it because they wanted to, and because users
desired it.

John Siracusa has a long memory, cares deeply about Mac design, and is not prone to hyperbole (putting it mildly). I’m not sure I agree with him that this is “the worst design-related thing Apple has ever done to Mac developers”, but it’s certainly on the short list for consideration. And, like Siracusa, I can’t think of any other design crime Apple has ever foisted on Mac developers that I’d argue (with Siracusa) was worse.

It’s one thing for Apple to force all of its own app icons into the same identical shape. That would be bad enough, because Apple’s own Mac apps are numerous and popular, and as the platform owner Apple necessarily sets the direction that many third-party apps follow. But it’s just downright spiteful to enforce it platform-wide. Apple decided they’re no longer going to create nice icons with unique, interesting, and most importantly, distinctive shapes — but they no longer allow third-party apps to either. It’s like Apple decided every single one of its own apps must wear a stupid-looking hat, and they put those stupid-looking hats on third-party apps too, whether the developers of those apps want them or not. Scratch that. Not hats but helmets. The mandatory squircle makes identifying apps at a glance harder in the same way that it’s difficult to identify individual people if they’re all wearing same-shaped helmets. Real helmets at least serve an important safety purpose. The squircles are like stupid unnecessary helmets.
To that point, Jim Nielsen draws an even better analogy — traffic signs:

Consistency for traffic signs! Let’s start by redesigning them all
to be the same shape.
Which was a sarcasm-dripping reply to his own previous post:

Shape isn’t everything, but it’s one tool to help provide
differentiation and uniqueness in icons. But not anymore.
Just the mere silhouette of the old Keynote icon is more recognizable, and thus more iconic, than any icon on any platform from Apple today.

No civil engineer would ever suggest changing yield and stop signs from their iconic triangles and octagons to identical squircles. The human visual system evolved to be remarkably good and quick at identifying shapes. The primary element of an app icon is the semantic meaning of its illustration. Color and shape are secondary. With the squircle mandate, Apple has removed shape from the equation.1 The purpose of icons is right there in their name: to be iconic. Shape was often the most iconic thing about an icon. Now it’s no part at all.

It makes no more sense than removing color. But Apple did that too! One of the purported reasons for the new icon guidelines across MacOS and iOS are the tinted and clear appearance options introduced last year with Liquid Glass and the OS 26 releases. These are both terrible ideas that remove color as a distinguishing factor, reducing ostensibly distinguishable icons into indistinguishable buttons. Adam Engst skewered the Clear and Tinted icon appearance options in a recent column at TidBITS, and ran a poll to see if anyone actually used them. Spoiler: nope.
App icons used to be exuberantly fun and so beautiful that they were the subject of two splendid coffee table books. This squircle shit is no fun at all, and ugly as sin.
Let’s go back.

With the new Creator Studio suite, Apple has largely (and for some apps, entirely) removed semantically meaningful illustrations from its own app icons. The only thing left to distinguish them is the color the crude squiggle inside the squircle. ↩︎

translations: Paul Kafasis 在 Rogue Amoeba 博客上一篇题为“Free the Icons”的文章中写道：

Apple 对图标形状的禁令，对于应用图标的可用性和创造力来说都是一种倒退。现在图标变得更难区分了，因为它们不再被允许具有独特性。但这在技术上没有任何理由。Apple 可以、也应该再次允许图标呈现各种形状。显然，Apple 内部的一些人已经认识到向 Liquid Glass 的过渡引入了一些错误。他们似乎也有权修复这些错误。在 Golden Gate 中对 Apple 自带图标的改进是一个令人欣慰的纠偏，备受赞誉的 Liquid Glass 不透明度滑块也是如此。现在也是时候纠正禁止图标形状这个错误了。Apple 应该停止强迫每个图标都变成同样的 squircle 形状。
我必须指出，squircle 本身并不是问题所在。如果是强制规定任何其他形状，比如 VisionOS 中的圆形，问题也是一样的。
John Siracusa：
“Squircle Jail”是 Apple 对 Mac 开发者做过的最糟糕的设计相关决策，而且很可能也是其在图标方面做过的最糟糕的决策，没有之一。这极其敌视开发者。如果 squircle 图标真的更好，那就让这种设计在市场上胜出。我们就是这样从经典的 Mac OS 图标风格过渡到更具照片写实感的 Mac OS X 图标风格的。开发者采用它是因为他们自己想这么做，也是因为用户有需求。
John Siracusa 记忆力极佳，对 Mac 设计极为关注，而且（毫不夸张地说）绝不是个喜欢夸大其词的人。我不确定是否同意他关于这是“Apple 对 Mac 开发者做过的最糟糕的设计相关决策”的说法，但它绝对名列前茅。而且，和 Siracusa 一样，我想不出 Apple 还曾把哪项“设计罪行”强加给 Mac 开发者，让我能（和 Siracusa 争论说）比这更糟。

Apple 强迫其自带的所有应用图标变成完全相同的形状是一回事。这本身就已经够糟了，因为 Apple 自带的 Mac 应用数量众多且广受欢迎，而作为平台所有者，Apple 必然会引领许多第三方应用跟随的方向。但在全平台强制执行这一规定，简直就是充满恶意。Apple 决定不再创建具有独特、有趣且最重要的是具有辨识度形状的好看图标了——而且他们也不再允许第三方应用这么做了。这就好比 Apple 决定它自己的每一个应用都必须戴上一顶难看的帽子，并且不管那些第三方应用的开发者愿不愿意，他们也给第三方应用戴上了这些难看的帽子。不，这种说法不准确。不是帽子，而是头盔。强制性的 squircle 让一眼认出应用变得更加困难，就像如果所有人都戴着相同形状的头盔，就很难认出具体的某个人一样。真正的头盔至少还有重要的安全作用。而 squircle 就像愚蠢且毫无必要的头盔。
说到这一点，Jim Nielsen 打了一个更绝妙的比方——交通标志：
为了交通标志的一致性！让我们先把它们全部重新设计成相同的形状吧。
这是他对自己上一篇帖子的回复，字里行间充满了讽刺：
形状不能决定一切，但它是帮助图标实现差异化和独特性的工具之一。但现在不是了。
仅仅是旧版 Keynote 图标的剪影，就比 Apple 如今在任何平台上的任何图标都更具辨识度，因而也更具标志性。

没有任何土木工程师会建议将让行和停车标志从标志性的三角形和八边形改成一模一样的方圆形。人类的视觉系统在进化中变得极其擅长且迅速地识别形状。应用图标的首要元素是其插画所传达的语义，颜色和形状都是次要的。然而，随着强制使用方圆形规定的出台，Apple 已经将形状从视觉等式中剔除了。图标（icon）的目的就体现在它的名字里：成为标志（iconic）。形状往往曾是图标最具标志性的部分，而现在却毫无用武之地。

这就和去除颜色一样毫无道理。但 Apple 确实也这么干了！跨 MacOS 和 iOS 的新版图标指南，其宣称的理由之一，是去年随 Liquid Glass 和 OS 26 版本引入的着色与透明外观选项。这两个都是糟糕透顶的主意，它们去除了颜色这一区分因素，把表面上还能区分的图标变成了难以分辨的按钮。Adam Engst 最近在 TidBITS 的专栏文章中猛烈抨击了透明和着色图标外观选项，并发起了一项投票，看看是否真的有人在使用它们。剧透一下：根本没人用。
应用图标曾经充满生机与乐趣，而且无比精美，以至于成为了两本精美画册的主题。这种方圆形的垃圾设计简直毫无乐趣可言，而且丑陋不堪。
让我们回到过去吧。
在全新的 Creator Studio 套件中，Apple 已经在很大程度上（对于某些应用甚至是完全）移除了其自身应用图标中具有语义的插画。剩下唯一能区分它们的，只有方圆形内部那粗糙曲线的颜色了。

articles.title: Kort geding aandeelhouders Solvinity
articles.titleZh: Solvinity 股东对荷兰政府提起的简易诉讼
articles.summary: Solvinity（DigiD背后的技术公司）的股东就其业务问题对负责数字经济和主权的荷兰副国务卿提起了简易判决诉讼。作者在法庭旁听了庭审，并发现许多在随后的主流媒体报道中被遗漏或淡化的关键细节。尽管包括 AD 和 NRC 在内的媒体进行了大规模报道，但新闻往往只关注表面冲突（例如政府拒绝收购该公司）。作者的核心观点是，亲自参与法庭旁听能揭示出比经过过滤的新闻报道更深层、更真实的内幕。
articles.summaryEn: Shareholders of Solvinity, the company behind DigiD, filed a preliminary injunction lawsuit against the Dutch State Secretary for Digital Economy and Sovereignty. The author attended the court hearing and noticed crucial details that were either omitted or downplayed in subsequent mainstream media coverage. Despite heavy reporting by major outlets like AD and NRC, the news largely focused on surface-level conflicts, such as the government's alleged refusal to buy the company. The author concludes that physically attending court proceedings reveals deeper insights that filtered news reports often miss.
articles.reason: 提供了一个难得的现场视角，揭示了主流媒体在报道 Solvinity/DigiD 重大法律纠纷时的盲点和信息过滤现象。

blocks.text: Gisteren deed ik op Mastodon live verslag van het kort geding van de aandeelhouders van Solvinity tegen de staatssecretaris van Digitale Economie en Soevereiniteit. Gek genoeg zag ik in de rechtbank dingen die ik later in het nieuws niet of weinig vernam.
Pers en media waren in grote getale op komen draven, wat leidde tot de volgende artikelen:
AD: Nederlandse overheid wilde bedrijf achter DigiD niet zelf kopen, stelt Solvinity in rechtbank
NRC: Met harde woorden vecht Solvinity, het bedrijf achter DigiD, het verbod op verkoop aan een Amerikaans bedrijf aan  (kadolink, laat weten als ‘ie niet meer werkt)
Nu.nl: DigiD-beheerder Solvinity houdt vol dat overname geen publieke risico’s vormt
BNR: “De Avondspits”, met ook een gesprek met mij.
Volkskrant: Staatssecretaris liet zich leiden door ‘mediahype’ bij overnameverbod Solvinity, meent Solvinity
Parool/ANP: Nederlandse overheid wilde Solvinity niet zelf kopen, stelt bedrijf in rechtbank
Trouw: Amerikaans bedrijf dat DigiD moet overnemen is volgens Solvinity ‘een veilig huis’
NOS: Solvinity wil onderzoek rond verbod op Amerikaanse overname via rechter heropenen
FD: Harde woorden bij rechtszaak overnameverbod Solvinity (kadolink, laat weten als ‘ie niet meer werkt)
De Rechtbank in Rotterdam, vrijwel gelegen in Metrohalte Wilhelminaplein, superhandig. Foto via de beeldbank van de rechtspraak

Deze rechtszaak gaat over iets heel specifieks. De staatssecretaris heeft de overname verboden en de huidige aandeelhouders hebben al bezwaar aangetekend. Dat zou eind september tot een uitspraak van de minister moeten leiden.

Maar, de aandeelhouders vinden dat te lang duren, en ze willen het overnameverbod nu al van tafel. Daarvoor kan je in Nederland een spoedprocedure starten bij de rechter, in dit geval een verzoek tot voorlopige voorziening. Deze procedure is beschreven in de 14e afdeling van het Wetboek van Burgerlijke Rechtsvordering.
Artikel 254: “In alle spoedeisende zaken waarin, gelet op de belangen van partijen, een onmiddellijke voorziening bij voorraad wordt vereist, is de voorzieningenrechter bevoegd deze te geven.”

Een kort geding draait om het spoedeisend belang. Want als dat er niet is begin je maar een gewone zaak waar wel tijd is voor uitgebreide bespreking en overweging. Dan heb je geen voorlopige voorziening nodig.
De eisende partij moet dit spoedeisend belang onderbouwen, anders verklaart de rechter de zaak niet-ontvankelijk.

Gedurende de zitting vroeg de rechter meerdere malen flink door over dit spoedeisend belang. Wat zou het probleem zijn voor de aandeelhouders om te moeten wachten tot september? En als de schade alleen financieel is, dan kan die in later stadium teruggevraagd woren. Is de schade onherstelbaar?
De aandeelhouders van Solvinity gaven hier geen goede antwoorden op, ook niet na doorvragen. Ze hameren erop hoe oneerlijk ze behandeld zijn door de overheid, en hoe lang de procedure al loopt.
Maar er komt geen goede onderbouwing voor het spoedeisend belang en waarom het niet kan wachten op het oordeel in september van het ministerie op het al ingediend bezwaar.

Aan het einde van het publieke deel van de rechtszaak geeft de rechter een ferme preview. Hij memoreert dat er echt een spoedeisend belang moet zijn, en dat als dat er niet is het besluit van de staatssecretaris wel HEEL erg onrechtmatig zou moeten zijn voor er sprake kan zijn van een voorziening. En hij laat doorschemeren dat beide criteria weleens niet gehaald zouden kunnen worden.
Tenzij er in het besloten gedeelte van de vergadering nog allemaal dingen onthuld zouden worden, overigens.

Later op de gang hoorde ik veel twijfels over het spoedeisend belang, en bevriende juristen vertelden me ook dat dit ook een hoge lat is om te halen. En dat als je advocaten in plaats van dat belang te onderbouwen beginnen over wat er in november 2025 allemaal gebeurde je er vermoedelijk niet gaat komen.
In de artikelen van de Volkskrant, NRC en AD (update: en nu.nl) wordt het spoedeisend belang genoemd, het beste in het stuk in het AD.

De overige artikelen rapporteren uitgebreid over wat Solvinity beweert over het onrecht wat ze aangedaan is, en dat de overheid zei dat dat best meeviel. En dat is op zich wel interessant allemaal, al leerden we weinig wat nog niet bekend was. Maar de zaak draaide er helemaal niet om of Solvinity nobele mensen zijn.

Het verbaast me wat dat de essentie van waar de zaak om ging zo weinig belicht is in de meeste artikelen. Is de schade de komende twee maanden zo groot dat het verbod op de verkoop onmiddellijk van tafel moet?
Verder ben ik natuurlijk heel blij met alle aandacht voor de zaak, dat was echt nuttig. Ook de stampvolle zaal is opgemerkt, wat iets zegt over het maatschappelijk belang wat wordt gehecht aan DigiD.
Mogelijk kunnen we het daar later in een bodemprocedure wel eens uitgebreid over gaan hebben!

PS: Over het belang van aandacht in de media, ik klaagde recent dat de verzamelde Nederlandse landelijke en regionale pers in totaal maar liefst twee alinea’s had geschreven over het stilleggen van de kerncentrale in Borssele wegens een lek ik in het nucleaire gedeelte. Dit vlak na de jaarlijkse inspectie en een maand-durende onderhoudsbeurt. Dit leek me gezien de (controversiële) wens van het kabinet om tot 5 nieuwe kerncentrales aan te leggen toch wel nieuwswaardig. Maar kennelijk niet. De pers bepaalt met haar keuzes in belangrijke mate waar we en de politiek het over hebben. Geen aandacht is geen debat, dus het boeit wel!

translations: 昨天，我在 Mastodon 上对 Solvinity 股东起诉数字经济与主权事务国务秘书的简易程序庭审进行了直播。奇怪的是，我在法庭上看到的一些情况，后来在新闻中却鲜有或根本没有报道。
大量媒体和记者蜂拥而至，催生了以下这些文章：
AD：Solvinity 在法庭上表示，荷兰政府本不想自己收购 DigiD 背后的公司
NRC：作为 DigiD 背后的公司，Solvinity 措辞强烈地反对将其出售给美国公司的禁令（链接，如果失效请告知）
Nu.nl：DigiD 运营商 Solvinity 坚称此次收购不会构成公共风险
BNR：“De Avondspits”节目，其中也包含对我的采访。
Volkskrant：Solvinity 认为，国务秘书在下达针对 Solvinity 的收购禁令时受到了“媒体炒作”的影响
Parool/ANP：该公司在法庭上表示，荷兰政府本不想自己收购 Solvinity
Trouw：据 Solvinity 称，即将收购 DigiD 的美国公司是“一家安全的机构”
NOS：Solvinity 希望通过法官重启针对美国收购禁令的调查
FD：关于 Solvinity 收购禁令诉讼中的激烈言辞（链接，如果失效请告知）
位于鹿特丹的法院，就在 Wilhelminaplein 地铁站旁边，超级方便。照片来自司法机构图片库。
这场诉讼针对的是一件非常具体的事情。国务秘书禁止了该收购案，而现有股东已经提出了异议。这应该会在九月底由部长做出裁决。
但是，股东们觉得这太费时间了，他们希望现在就能把收购禁令撤销。为此，在荷兰你可以向法官启动紧急程序，在本案中也就是申请临时救济。该程序在《民事诉讼法典》第 14 编中有明确规定。
第 254 条：“在所有考虑到当事人利益而需要立即提供初步救济的紧急案件中，简易法庭法官有权提供此类救济。”
简易程序的核心在于紧急利益。因为如果没有紧急性，你完全可以启动一个常规案件，有的是时间进行详细的讨论和审议。那样你就不需要临时救济了。
原告方必须证明这种紧急利益，否则法官将以不予受理为由驳回案件。
在庭审过程中，法官多次就这一紧急利益进行了深入盘问。对于股东来说，等到九月份会有什么问题？如果损害纯粹是财务上的，那可以在后期追偿。这种损害是不可挽回的吗？
Solvinity 的股东们对此没有给出很好的回答，即使在追问之后也是如此。他们只是一再强调政府对待他们有多么不公，以及整个程序已经持续了多长时间。
但他们并没有为紧急利益提供充分的理由，也没有解释为什么不能等待部委在九月份对已提交的异议做出裁决。
在庭审公开部分的最后，法官给出了明确的预示。他提醒道，必须确实存在紧急利益，而且如果不存在，那么国务秘书的决定必须是非常极其不合法的，才能下达临时救济。他还暗示，这两个条件可能都无法满足。
除非在此次会议的闭门环节中还会披露其他内情，不过话又说回来。
后来在走廊里，我听到许多关于“紧急利益”的质疑，相熟的律师也告诉我这是一个很高的门槛。如果你的律师不去论证这一紧急利益，反而开始扯2025年11月发生的一堆事，那大概率是行不通的。
在《人民报》（Volkskrant）、《新鹿特丹商报》（NRC）和《共同日报》（AD）（更新：以及 now.nl）的报道中都提到了紧急利益，其中 AD 的报道写得最好。
其余的报道则长篇大论地讲述了 Solvinity 声称自身遭受的不公，以及政府方面表示情况其实并没有那么糟。这些内容本身确实挺有意思，尽管我们并没有从中了解到什么此前未知的新信息。但这起案件的核心根本就不在于 Solvinity 的人是否高尚。
令我惊讶的是，大多数报道都极少提及这起案件的核心争议：未来两个月内造成的损失是否真的大到必须立即将销售禁令撤下台面？
当然，我也非常高兴这起案件能获得如此多的关注，这确实很有意义。现场座无虚席的盛况也引起了人们的注意，这反映出社会各界对 DigiD 赋予了极高的重视。
也许在日后的实质性诉讼程序中，我们还有机会对此展开详尽的探讨！

附言：关于媒体关注度的重要性，我最近抱怨过，荷兰全国性和地区性媒体加起来，关于波尔瑟勒（Borssele）核电站因核设施区域发生泄漏而停机的报道，总共才写了两段话。而这恰好发生在年度检查和长达一个月的维护之后。考虑到内阁（备受争议的）新建5座核电站的计划，这似乎相当具有新闻价值。但显然媒体不这么认为。媒体通过其新闻选题，在很大程度上决定了我们和政界讨论的焦点。没有关注就没有辩论，所以这确实挺引人深思的！

articles.title: A full body MRI earns you a year of smoking
articles.titleZh: 做一次全身 MRI 扫描的风险相当于抽了一年的烟
articles.summary: 全身 MRI 扫描虽然常被宣传为高级的预防性健康检查，但其带来的潜在健康风险极高。文章指出，进行一次全身 MRI 检查所承受的累积风险，实际上等同于连续吸烟一整年。为了具象化这种隐性危险，作者将其与一系列极限高危活动进行了等效对比，包括高危孕产、攀登马特洪峰、骑摩托车行驶一万公里、两次定点跳伞，甚至是乌克兰前线的一天。这表明对于无症状的健康人群而言，盲目进行全身 MRI 筛查的相对风险被严重低估了。
articles.summaryEn: Despite being marketed as advanced preventive healthcare, full-body MRI scans carry surprisingly high health risks. The author points out that the cumulative risk of undergoing one full-body MRI scan is practically equivalent to smoking for an entire year. To contextualize this hidden danger, the article equates the risk to participating in extreme activities such as a high-risk pregnancy, summiting the Matterhorn, riding a motorcycle for 10,000 kilometers, or doing two BASE jumps. This comparison highlights that the relative dangers of indiscriminate full-body scans for asymptomatic people are severely underestimated.
articles.reason: 通过生动且极具冲击力的等效对比，打破了公众对“预防性全身 MRI 扫描绝对安全无害”的盲目迷信。

blocks.text: Alternative titles:
… earns you a high-risk pregnancy
… earns you an ascent of Matterhorn
… earns you 10,000 km on a motorcycle
… earns you two base jumps
… earns you a day on the frontline in Ukraine
These are all about equivalent to the risk of one year of smoking.

I’m skeptical of submitting asymptomatic people to medical tests. Almost any
time I look into the evidentiary power of medical tests, I’m struck by how much
work is performed by the base rate. The tests only work because we perform them
on people who appear sick, i.e. have a higher probability of actually being sick
in the first place. If we would perform them on seemingly-healthy people we
would get nonsensical results.11 Note that this is not a criticism of the
tests. They are optimised for the thing they need to do.

Thus it was with interest I read Scott Alexander’s breakdown of the benefits and
costs of a routine full-body mri as a way of screening for cancer. However, I
felt like the conclusions weren’t put into an understandable context. Here’s my
attempt at doing so.

First, a quick recap of the main points of the article. I’ll ignore the
exorbitant financial costs of us healthcare, and focus on the benefit and cost
in terms of health. This is measured in quality-adjusted life years, or
qalys. Of the hypothetical thousand people who get scanned, the estimation is
that

680 people will be fine, and this costs them only the doctor’s visit, which is
around 3 hours, or 0.0003 qalys.

296 people will undergo additional waiting and testing unnecessarily, at a
total cost of 0.02 qalys coming from side effects, anxiety, and patient
time.

10 people will have unnecessary biopsies on top of the additional waiting and
testing above, bringing their total cost to 0.06 qalys.

6 people will detect a real problem, but in a way that doesn’t help them.
We’ll count this as no benefit, but also no cost.22 They would probably have
gone through this circus eventually anyway.

4 people will benefit from early detection already at the mri stage, and
gain an average of 4 qalys from this, and at a cost of 0.007 qalys after
patient time and side effects, this is still a gain of 3.99 qalys.

4 people will benefit from early detection only after additional rounds of
testing. They still gain the 4 qalys but their cost is ten more hours of
patient time and some additional anxiety. It still ends up being a net benefit
of 3.99 qalys.

Tallying up the costs and benefits into an expected value, we get a net benefit
of 0.025 qalys per person, after accounting for medical time.33 This is the
figure Scott Alexander reports as “25” in sum across all 1000 people. I just
didn’t find its very clear so I had to replicate it to make sense of it. This
doesn’t tell me a whole lot, because my intuition for qalys is weak. How
strongly should I prefer an intervention with a net benefit of 0.025 qalys
over other things I might do with my time? No idea!

However! When marketing the effect of global health interventions, a count of 27
qalys is typically considered “a life saved”. A life also happens to be a
million micromorts, and I have a much better intuition for micromorts! When we
run that maths in reverse, we get a very cheeky exchange rate between qalys
and micromorts:

One qaly is 37,000 micromorts.44 The equivalence between 27 qalys and
a life saved is based on global demographics. For people in developed countries,
where the life expectation is longer, a qaly probably corresponds to a lower
number of micromorts – probably around 30,000 or so.

Thus, an intervention that has an expected benefit of 0.025 qalys – like a
routine full-body mri – corresponds to an intervention that has a benefit of
926 micromorts. The alternative titles indicate activities that carry roughly a
risk of 1000 micromorts:
a year of smoking,
a high-risk pregnancy,
an ascent of Matterhorn,
riding 10,000 km on a motorcycle,
two base jumps, and
one day on the frontline in Ukraine.

So the same effort you would expend to get out of those activities on account of
their risk, the same effort you should be willing to expend to get a full-body mri.

Note the on account of their risk phrasing. I have no interest in doing any
number of base jumps and will work hard to get out of doing them, but that’s
because I wouldn’t enjoy the activity, not because I’m worried about the risk.
If I was put in a situation where it seemed like I had to perform two base
jumps to reunite with my family, I would spend some effort on finding
alternative ways of getting there, but perhaps not all that much before I decide
to just eat the base jumps and getting it over with.

translations: 备选标题：
……相当于让你经历一次高危妊娠
……相当于让你攀登一次马特洪峰
……相当于让你骑摩托车行驶一万公里
……相当于让你进行两次定点跳伞
……相当于让你在乌克兰前线待上一天
这些大致等同于吸烟一年的风险。
我对让无症状人群接受医学检查持怀疑态度。几乎每次我研究医学检查的证据效力时，都会惊讶于基础概率在其中发挥的巨大作用。这些检查之所以有效，仅仅是因为我们在看似生病的人（即一开始实际患病的概率就更高的人）身上进行这些检查。如果我们在看似健康的人身上进行检查，就会得到毫无意义的结果。11 请注意，这并不是对检查本身的批评。它们已经针对其需要完成的目标进行了优化。
因此，当我读到 Scott Alexander 关于将常规全身 MRI 作为癌症筛查手段的成本效益分析时，我对此非常感兴趣。然而，我觉得文章的结论并没有被置于一个易于理解的背景中。以下是我尝试进行的一些背景补充。
首先，快速回顾一下该文章的要点。我将忽略美国医疗保健高昂的财务成本，而专注于健康方面的收益和成本。这是以质量调整生命年（quality-adjusted life years，简称 QALYs）来衡量的。在假设接受扫描的一千人中，估计情况如下：
680人将安然无恙，他们只需付出看医生的时间成本，大约为3小时，即 0.0003 QALYs。
296人将经历不必要的额外等待和检查，其产生的副作用、焦虑情绪以及患者时间成本总计为 0.02 QALYs。
10人除了上述的额外等待和检查外，还将接受不必要的活检，使其总成本达到 0.06 QALYs。
6人将查出真正的问题，但查出的方式对他们并无帮助。我们将此算作既无收益也无成本。22 反正他们最终可能也得经历这一番折腾。
4人将在 MRI 阶段就受益于早期发现，并由此平均获得 4 QALYs 的收益，扣除患者时间和副作用造成的 0.007 QALYs 成本后，仍有 3.99 QALYs 的净收益。
4人只有在经过额外的几轮检查后才会受益于早期发现。他们依然能获得 4 QALYs 的收益，但其成本是额外十小时的患者时间以及更多的焦虑。最终算下来依然是 3.99 QALYs 的净收益。

将成本和收益汇总为期望值，并在计入医疗时间成本后，我们得到的人均净收益为 0.025 QALYs。33 这正是 Scott Alexander 在汇总所有 1000 人时给出的“25”这个数字。我只是觉得那个表述不够清晰，所以不得不自己重新计算一遍以理解其含义。但这对我没有太多指导意义，因为我对 QALYs 的直觉感知很弱。相比于用我的时间去做其他事情，我到底应该多倾向于选择这项净收益为 0.025 QALYs 的干预措施？我毫无头绪！
然而！在宣传全球健康干预措施的效果时，通常将 27 QALYs 视为“拯救了一条生命”。而一条生命恰好等于一百万个微死亡率（micromorts），我对微死亡率的直觉感知要好得多！当我们把这个数学计算反过来，就会得到 QALYs 和微死亡率之间一个非常巧妙的换算比率：
1个 qaly 等于 37,000 个 micromorts。44 27个 qalys 相当于挽救一条生命，这是基于全球人口统计数据得出的。对于预期寿命较长的发达国家的人来说，1个 qaly 可能对应更少的 micromorts——大概在 30,000 左右。
因此，一项预期收益为 0.025 qalys 的干预措施——例如常规的全身 MRI——相当于一项收益为 926 micromorts 的干预措施。以下项目表明了风险大约为 1000 micromorts 的活动：
吸烟一年，
一次高危妊娠，
攀登一次马特洪峰，
骑摩托车行驶 10,000 公里，
两次定点跳伞，以及
在乌克兰前线待一天。
因此，考虑到风险，你愿意花多少精力去避免上述活动，就应该愿意花同样的精力去做一次全身 MRI。
请注意“考虑到风险”这一措辞。我对进行任何次数的定点跳伞都毫无兴趣，并且会努力避免去做，但那是因为我不喜欢这项活动，而不是因为我担心风险。如果我处于一种似乎必须完成两次定点跳伞才能与家人团聚的境地，我会花一些精力去寻找其他团聚的替代方法，但或许在决定直接硬着头皮跳完、把事情了结之前，我并不会花太多精力。

articles.title: Ray Kassar, former Atari CEO
articles.titleZh: 前雅达利 CEO：雷·卡萨尔
articles.summary: 雷·卡萨尔曾在 1978 年至 1983 年期间担任知名游戏公司雅达利的总裁及首席执行官。他于 1928 年出生，并于 2017 年在佛罗里达州离世，享年 89 岁。他最初是由雅达利的母公司华纳兄弟聘用来接管并管理公司业务的。作为雅达利历史上最具争议且最关键时期的领导者之一，他的商业决策和管理风格对早期电子游戏产业的兴衰产生了深远影响。
articles.summaryEn: Ray Kassar served as the president and later CEO of the iconic video game company Atari Inc. from 1978 to 1983. Born in 1928, he passed away in Vero Beach, Florida, at the age of 89 in 2017. He was originally hired by Atari's parent company, Warner Bros., to oversee and manage the business operations. As a key executive during one of Atari's most crucial and controversial periods, his decisions left a lasting impact on the trajectory of the early video game industry.
articles.reason: 简要梳理了雅达利早期关键领导人的生平，是了解早期电子游戏产业兴衰史不可或缺的人物背景资料。

blocks.text: Raymond Edward Kassar was born January 2, 1928 and died December 10, 2017, aged 89, in Vero Beach, Florida. Ray Kassar was president, and later CEO, of Atari Inc. from 1978 to 1983. Atari’s parent company, Warner Bros, hired him as president of Atari’s consumer division in February 1978 after he spent 26 years at Burlington Industries, a textile maker.
Ray Kassar’s rise at Atari

In November 1978, Warner fired Atari co-founder Nolan Bushnell. By some accounts, it was a disagreement over Atari’s future. By other accounts, it was a dispute over how much time Bushnell spent at the company. Bushnell was a serial entrepreneur with other business interests such as the Chuck E. Cheese pizza chain, and Warner likely had concerns about his commitment to Atari.

Warner then promoted Kassar to CEO. Under Kassar’s leadership, Atari’s culture shifted from a focus on engineering to a focus on business, with mixed results. The culture at Burlington Industries had been one of order, organization, and efficiency. Kassar tried to replicate that at Atari. After calling Atari programmers “high-strung prima donnas” on the record in an interview with the San Jose Mercury News in 1979, Atari employees unaffectionately called him the “sock king” and the “towel czar.”

Kassar was notoriously unpopular with Atari engineers, but the business partisans didn’t universally fall into line with Kassar either. Atari’s upper management suffered severe turnover rates. Many blamed Ray Kassar’s autocratic management style, but Kassar was not held accountable.

According to the Nov 28, 1983 issue of Infoworld, Nolan Bushnell told Warner that Kassar was the wrong man for the job. “I told [Warner co-president Emanuel Gerard] he was the wrong man. I didn’t think Kassar could get along with engineers. He couldn’t get down on the floor with them… You’ve got to have enough faith in them to say, ‘I don’t know what you’re talking about. Here’s some money, go show me.'”

This stood in sharp contrast with some of his peers. For example, future Atari CEO Jack Tramiel would fraternize with engineers, consider ideas from them, and even let them joke with him, even though he also had a reputation for being hard to work for.
Kassar’s disputes with Atari engineers

Atari its greatest success during Kassar’s time as CEO, growing Atari’s sales from $75 million in 1977 to over $2.2 billion in 1980. But the stifling atmosphere and lack of royalties or recognition to the individual game designers angered employees. Many quit. During this period, nearly all members of the original Atari staff, including Al Alcorn and Jay Miner, quit or were fired. This cut off Atari’s pipeline of new ideas, which caused problems as the Atari 2600 game console and Atari 800 home computer aged. As competitors caught up, Atari didn’t have anything new to counter with.

The most infamous example of Kassar’s attitude toward employees was his dispute with Atari developers. Four programmers were unsatisfied with their paychecks. They believed the salary they were making was inappropriate for someone designing the games that made the company millions of dollars. They wanted a small royalty. But when they asked Kassar, David Crane recalls that Kassar responded, “You are no more important to that game than the guy on the assembly line who puts it together.”
Crane, along with Bob Whitehead, Larry Kaplan, and Alan Miller resigned from Atari and formed their own company, Activision, becoming the first ever third-party developer.

In May 1982, Atari released the highly popular and successful game Yars’ Revenge for the Atari 2600. Howard Scott Warshaw, the game’s designer, got the names “Yar” and “Razak” by jokingly spelling “Ray Kassar” backwards. Warshaw called the game “Ray’s revenge on Activision.”
But the revenge proved short lived. Activision had a few more good years left in it. Kassar only had a few good months left.
Atari’s fall from grace in late 1982

Kassar’s problems caught up with him, and Atari, by the fall of 1982. The year 1982 started out spectacularly. Atari earned more than $300 million in the first three quarters, shattering its previous records for a full year. But Atari missed its targets for the critical fourth quarter. Making matters worse, Kassar sold 5,000 shares of stock in Warner Communications only 23 minutes before the report went public. Atari’s miss sent Warner stock into a free fall, losing 40 percent of its value.

The Securities and Exchange Commission accused Kassar and then-Atari vice-president Dennis Groth of illegally trading stock with insider knowledge. Kassar settled, returning his profits without acknowledging guilt or innocence.
Letting Nintendo slip away

A final stain on Kassar’s legacy with Atari was his missed opportunity with Nintendo. Nintendo wanted Atari to partner to bring its Famicom console to the United States, but a dispute with Nintendo over its licensing of Donkey Kong caused Kassar to cut off communication with Nintendo. Nintendo later launched the very successful Nintendo Entertainment System without Atari, partnering with toy companies like Worlds of Wonder and Mattel to help distribute it worldwide.
The end of the line for Kassar and Atari

Things only got worse in 1983. That year, Atari lost $45.6 million in its first quarter and a stunning $310 million in its second. Investors went from thinking video games were a new industry to thinking of them like a passing fad, like the Rubik’s Cube. Atari’s woes took the whole industry down with it.

Whether Atari fired Kassar or he resigned depends who you ask, but Kassar left Atari on July 7, 1983. Warner hired former Phillip Morris executive James J. Morgan as CEO of Atari in September 1983, and Warner sold Atari to Commodore founder Jack Tramiel less than a year later.
Kassar never held another executive position again. He worked as a private investor and sat on the Board of the American Hospital of Paris Foundation.
25 years and two days after Warner announced its earnings miss and Kassar sold 5,000 shares of stock prompting an SEC investigation, Kassar died at the age of 89, in Florida.

But about that Yar’s Revenge thing. I’m not convinced Ray Kassar ever got revenge on Activision, Atari, Nintendo, or any other tech company he had a beef with. But maybe he got revenge on Warner. Warner and its successor, Time Warner, never mixed well with technology companies. See the disastrous AOL-Time Warner merger for a nice example.

translations: 雷蒙德·爱德华·卡萨尔（Raymond Edward Kassar）生于1928年1月2日，于2017年12月10日在佛罗里达州维罗海滩去世，享年89岁。1978年至1983年间，雷·卡萨尔（Ray Kassar）担任 Atari 公司总裁，后出任 CEO。1978年2月，在纺织制造商伯灵顿工业公司（Burlington Industries）工作了26年后，Atari 的母公司华纳兄弟（Warner Bros）聘请他担任 Atari 消费品部门总裁。
雷·卡萨尔在 Atari 的崛起
1978年11月，华纳解雇了 Atari 联合创始人诺兰·布什内尔（Nolan Bushnell）。有传言称，这是因为双方在 Atari 的未来发展方向上存在分歧；也有说法认为，这源于布什内尔在公司投入的时间不足。布什内尔是一名连续创业者，还有许多其他商业利益，例如 Chuck E. Cheese 披萨连锁店，因此华纳很可能对他投入在 Atari 的精力感到担忧。

随后华纳将卡萨尔提拔为 CEO。在卡萨尔的领导下，Atari 的企业文化从重工程转向了重商业，结果毁誉参半。伯灵顿工业公司的文化讲究秩序、组织和效率，卡萨尔试图在 Atari 复制这种文化。1979年，在接受《圣何塞信使报》（San Jose Mercury News）采访时，他公开称 Atari 的程序员是“高度紧张的特权人物（prima donnas）”，此后 Atari 员工便充满调侃地叫他“袜子大王”或“毛巾沙皇”。
众所周知，卡萨尔在 Atari 工程师中极不受欢迎，但商业派员工也并非完全服从他。Atari 的高层管理人员流失率极高。许多人将其归咎于雷·卡萨尔独断专行的管理风格，但他并未因此受到问责。
根据1983年11月28日出版的《Infoworld》杂志报道，诺兰·布什内尔曾告诉华纳，卡萨尔并不适合这个职位。“我告诉[华纳联合总裁伊曼纽尔·杰拉德（Emanuel Gerard）]他选错人了。我认为卡萨尔无法与工程师们相处。他无法放下身段和他们打成一片……你必须对他们有足够的信心，能够对他们说：‘我不知道你们在说什么，这是经费，去做出成果给我看。’”
这与他的某些同行形成了鲜明对比。例如，后来成为 Atari CEO 的杰克·特拉梅尔（Jack Tramiel）就会与工程师们打成一片，倾听他们的想法，甚至允许他们和自己开玩笑，尽管他也以难以共事而闻名。
卡萨尔与 Atari 工程师的争端

在卡萨尔担任 CEO 期间，Atari 取得了巨大的成功，销售额从1977年的7500万美元增长到1980年的22亿美元以上。但令人窒息的氛围以及对个人游戏设计师缺乏版税或认可，激怒了员工，许多人因此辞职。在此期间，包括阿尔·阿尔康（Al Alcorn）和杰伊·迈纳（Jay Miner）在内的几乎所有 Atari 初创团队成员都辞职或被解雇。这切断了 Atari 新创意的来源，并随着 Atari 2600 游戏机和 Atari 800 家用电脑的老化引发了危机。当竞争对手迎头赶上时，Atari 却拿不出任何新产品来应对。
卡萨尔对待员工态度中最臭名昭著的例子，就是他与 Atari 开发人员的争端。四名程序员对他们的薪水感到不满。他们认为，对于设计出为公司赚取数百万美元游戏的人来说，他们的薪水实在是不相称。他们想要少量的版税。但当他们向卡萨尔提出要求时，大卫·克莱恩（David Crane）回忆说，卡萨尔回答道：“对于游戏而言，你们并不比流水线上组装它的工人更重要。”
克莱恩连同鲍勃·怀特海德（Bob Whitehead）、拉里·卡普兰（Larry Kaplan）和艾伦·米勒（Alan Miller）一起从 Atari 辞职，成立了自己的公司 Activision，成为了有史以来第一家第三方游戏开发商。
1982年5月，Atari 为 Atari 2600 发布了广受欢迎且大获成功的游戏《Yars' Revenge》。该游戏的设计师 Howard Scott Warshaw 通过开玩笑地将“Ray Kassar”倒序拼写，得到了“Yar”和“Razak”这两个名字。Warshaw 将这款游戏称为“Ray 对 Activision 的复仇”。
但这场复仇被证明是短暂的。Activision 还迎来了几年的辉煌时期，而 Kassar 却只剩下几个月的好日子了。
1982年底 Atari 跌下神坛

到了1982年秋天，Kassar 的问题终于反噬了他自己以及 Atari。1982年的开局可谓辉煌。Atari 在前三个季度赚取了超过3亿美元的利润，打破了其全年的历史最高纪录。但 Atari 在关键的第四季度却未能达成目标。更糟糕的是，在财报公开前仅23分钟，Kassar 卖出了5000股 Warner Communications 的股票。Atari 的业绩未达标导致 Warner 股票暴跌，市值蒸发了40%。
美国证券交易委员会（SEC）指控 Kassar 及时任 Atari 副总裁 Dennis Groth 利用内幕消息进行非法股票交易。Kassar 最终选择和解，退还了其获利，但既未承认有罪也未否认无罪。
与 Nintendo 失之交臂

Kassar 在 Atari 职业生涯中的最后一个污点，就是错失了与 Nintendo 合作的良机。Nintendo 本希望与 Atari 合作，将其 Famicom 游戏机引入美国，但由于双方在《Donkey Kong》的授权问题上发生争执，导致 Kassar 中断了与 Nintendo 的沟通。后来，Nintendo 在没有 Atari 参与的情况下，成功推出了大获成功的 Nintendo Entertainment System（NES），并与 Worlds of Wonder 和 Mattel 等玩具公司合作，协助其向全球发行。
Kassar 与 Atari 的末路
到了1983年，情况变得更加糟糕。那一年，Atari 在第一季度亏损了4560万美元，在第二季度更是惊人地亏损了3.1亿美元。投资者们的看法发生了转变，他们不再认为电子游戏是一个新兴的产业，而是将其视为像魔方（Rubik's Cube）一样转瞬即逝的狂热。Atari 的困境也拖垮了整个游戏行业。
关于 Atari 是解雇了 Kassar 还是他主动辞职，不同的人有不同的说法，但 Kassar 确实于1983年7月7日离开了 Atari。1983年9月，Warner 聘请了前 Phillip Morris 高管 James J. Morgan 担任 Atari 的首席执行官，而不到一年后，Warner 就将 Atari 卖给了 Commodore 的创始人 Jack Tramiel。
此后，Kassar 再也没有担任过任何高管职位。他成为了一名私人投资者，并担任了 American Hospital of Paris Foundation 的董事会成员。
在 Warner 宣布业绩未达标且 Kassar 卖出5000股股票引发 SEC 调查的25年零两天后，Kassar 在佛罗里达州去世，享年89岁。
但关于《Yar's Revenge》这件事，我不太相信 Ray Kassar 曾对 Activision、Atari、Nintendo 或任何其他他有过节的技术公司进行过复仇。不过，也许他真的对 Warner 复仇了。Warner 及其继任者 Time Warner 与科技公司向来格格不入。灾难性的 AOL 与 Time Warner 合并案就是一个很好的例子。
David Farquhar 是一名计算机安全专家、企业家和作家。自1991年以来，他一直从事专业的计算机写作，所以当那些复古计算机还属于新鲜事物时，他就在撰写关于它们的文章了。自1994年起，他一直在 IT 行业担任专业职务，并自2013年起专注于漏洞管理领域。他拥有 Security+ 和 CISSP 认证。如今，他每周撰写五篇博客，主要探讨1975年至2000年间的复古计算机和复古游戏。
